inventory.name: form_submission member of a prerender speculation rule

notes: Surface: the form_submission member of a prerender speculation rule and the activation-matching rule that gives it meaning. TWO rows, not three. The first version of this contract kept a THIRD row for the eligibility check, and that was wrong in the way this campaign exists to catch: the check is a CONSEQUENCE of the field, not a distinct surface, so two of its cells pointed at fragments that did not document that dimension for that item - its context cell pointed at the lifecycle section, which never mentions form-action or CSP, and its syntax and examples cells inherited the field's JSON and live example, neither of which demonstrates the check. Worse, the notes that rejected a fourth row for the prefetch-discard scope used the argument that applies exactly to the eligibility row. Recognising that a row has no distinct content is the fix; keeping the row and marking its cells 'documented' is the mislabelling this catalogue's contracts are meant to prevent. The eligibility content is not lost: the field's outputs cell carries the 'Effect when true' and 'Eligibility' table rows, and the securityPrivacy cell carries the framing (a resource argument, not a privacy property, in the explainer's own words). Zero 'not-applicable' cells remain, and that is a judgement rather than a default: for these two rows each of the nine questions has real, sourced content on the page - the boolean value contract and its non-boolean handling (inputs, errors), the rule-kind scope (context), the prepared-then-retained-then-activated path (lifecycle), and the navigation-type matching with its refusal mode (the activation row's inputs/outputs/errors). NOT settled in the sources and recorded as such on the page: whether list-only enforcement reaches the parser. The explainer intends list rules because document rules match links rather than buttons, but the PR diff propagates the member through the per-link document-rule path as well, so the page's hedge is the accurate form and this contract does not upgrade it to a guarantee. The declared-surface rule (gendn-4kq) has nothing to check here: this page declares no WebIDL, its surface is JSON, and the syntax block is a JSON example rather than an interface.
